issues.body: Unchanged from round 1; re-verified against the tree. The old text was a hedged claim carrying a re-check pointer ('the consequences of triple terms for canonicalization are unsettled upstream (see w3c/rdf-star-wg#114)'). The new text — 'no W3C RDF-1.2 dataset-canonicalization specification exists' — is a strictly stronger, absolute, undated assertion about the outside world, and the same diff deletes the only reference a reader or future agent could follow to confirm it (crates/sparq-canon/src/rdf12.rs:5-12 now keeps only the [RDFC-1.0] definition). Two consequences: (a) if the W3C RDF 1.2 WG has, or later has, an editor's draft / Working Draft / chartered canonicalization deliverable, 'no specification exists' reads as false where 'unsettled upstream' would still have been true, and nothing in the doc says where to look; (b) the citation was not removed for gate reasons — scripts/banned-terminology.json:200 explicitly allow-lists 'rdf-star-wg' as a legitimate proper-noun/URL citation, and skills/terminology/SKILL.md:124-125 warns that 'Silent flattening of a precise prior-art reference is as much a documentation defect as leaving a deprecated term in current-state copy.' The identical wording lands in Cargo.toml, README.md, lib.rs and SKILL.md, so this applies to all five surfaces. Non-blocking: no behavioural, soundness or security consequence, and the non-standard/opt-in/fail-closed labels are intact.
issues.fix_hint: Either keep the tracking link alongside the new phrasing (e.g. '... no W3C RDF-1.2 dataset-canonicalization specification exists; the underlying question is tracked at w3c/rdf-star-wg#114'), restoring the '[w3c/rdf-star-wg#114]: https://github.com/w3c/rdf-star-wg/issues/114' reference definition in crates/sparq-canon/src/rdf12.rs; or make the claim bounded and checkable: '... no W3C RDF-1.2 dataset-canonicalization Recommendation or Working Draft as of 2026-08'. Apply the same edit to the other four surfaces so the wording stays single-voiced.
issues.title: Cited hedge replaced by an undated, uncited absolute claim about external W3C state (unchanged from round 1)

issues.body: Unchanged from round 1; re-verified. The shipped surfaces now say 'no W3C RDF 1.2 dataset-canonicalization specification exists' (crates/sparq-canon/README.md:54), while research/rdf-canon-rdf12-triple-terms-upstream.md:15-16 (and lines 27, 42, 188) and bead sq-hslb still frame the same fact as 'currently undefined / unsettled upstream (w3c/rdf-star-wg#114)'. That is defensible — research/ records are dated historical artefacts and are deliberately not kept in lockstep — but a reader moving from the README to the design record meets two characterisations of the same upstream state with no bridge between them. Cosmetic only.
issues.fix_hint: No change required if the divergence is intentional. If a single voice is wanted, reuse one phrasing in both places, or add one clause to the README/SKILL note pointing at research/rdf-canon-rdf12-triple-terms-upstream.md as the record of the upstream questions this profile raised.

verdict.summary: Round 2.
